title_en: The Steam Machine Is Now Available Without a Subscription, But a Price Increase Is Likely Come January
summary_en: Back when the Steam Machine first came out in June, it was in short supply, due to the limited amount of hardware Valve was able to get its hands on (thanks, RAM crisis). But now, about 5 months after launch, you can finally just buy a Steam Machine.
body_en:
When the Steam Machine first came out in June, it was in short supply, due to the limited amount of hardware Valve was able to get its hands on (thanks, RAM crisis). Now, about 5 months after launch, you can finally just buy a Steam Machine.
Valve put out a blog post on November 19 giving an update on Steam Machine reservations, revealing that it had just finished out sending purchase invites to anyone on the reservation list for the 2TB model. The 512GB version, though, is now available to purchase on the Steam store page without a reservation. However, it looks like Valve doesn't have the components on hand to make the 2TB model available in the same way.
According to Valve's blog, the ongoing memory shortage is particularly impacting the 2TB Steam Machine because of its much larger drive. The company says the amount of people on the waitlist for the 2TB Machine exceeds what there were able to make, and while it's going to make more, it's going to be at a limited rate.
Still, Valve was able to get through its 512GB Steam Machine waitlist much earlier than expected. When the mini PC launched, some people were placed on the waitlist with an expected order time of 2027. Luckily, the new year hasn't ticked over, and the Machine is now available to buy for anyone that wants it... but there is a possibility that Valve will sell through its entire supply.
Valve does say that it's going to continue to build the Machine, but it sounds like the production run is going to be limited. It says that "memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result, we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them."
It's no secret that the RAM crisis has been particularly unforgiving to the Steam Machine, and it's not likely to let up in the near future. Samsung told investors in an earnings call last month that it expects supply to be more constrained next year, and all three of the major RAM manufacturers have sold through their manufacturing capacity through next year.
It doesn't seem likely that the memory and storage costs that are limiting how many Steam Machines Valve can make will let up at all in the near future. From the way that blog post ended by saying it doesn't know how many Steam Machines it can make or how expensive they're going to be, it's very likely that the mini PC is either going to get a hearty price rise in January, or just be discontinued until Valve can make a followup when prices go down. Either way, it's a shame – the Steam Machine is an excellent little computer, and the RAM crisis unfortunately made it a non-starter for a lot of people, due to the price.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her  @Jackiecobra
